summary.assessment: The model is reliable on single-panel charts whose numbers are printed (B1 exact; the C5 pies are exact too, but the engine read those without calling the model) and gives usable approximate readings of one simple unlabelled panel (B4 forest plot, all centres within 1.7 % of the axis range). Its typical failure is structural: every multi-panel data figure lost panels, either merged under one axis (B2, B3, C4), merged or mislabelled (B5), reduced to a fragment (C3) or left 'not read' (6 panels of B5, panel 4 of C1), and that is where most of the 560 truth values went missing or became wrong. Where it does measure positions, the marks tend to land below the true mark (A3 centres 0.01-0.03 low, C1 bars 0.04-0.07 low), and where no axis is calibrated it returns rounded guesses with invented symmetric whiskers or bounds (B5, C4, B4). On the five no-data figures it never invents a number, but it never returns a clean empty result either: three get an empty 'stacked_bar' shell and two (A4, A5) get rows with null values, 76 of them on the ECG traces after 667 s. It also ignored printed numbers when they sat in legends of a multi-panel figure (B3: 15 AUROC values, none read). It can be trusted on a single-panel bar chart with printed labels and, to about two significant digits, on a single-panel interval plot; multi-panel figures, dense line or stacked-bar charts and box plots should not be taken from it as they are.
